🚀 12 Data Engineering Concepts You MUST Know Before Your Next Interview (2026)
If you’re preparing for a Data Engineer interview, don’t just revise tools — master the core concepts.
 Most candidates fail not because of syntax — but because of weak fundamentals.
Save this checklist before your next interview 👇1️⃣ ETL vs ELT — When to transform before load vs after load
 2️⃣ Data Warehousing vs Data Lake — Use cases, cost, schema strategy
 3️⃣ Batch vs Streaming Pipelines — Latency vs throughput tradeoffs
 4️⃣ Star vs Snowflake Schema — Query performance vs normalization
 5️⃣ Partitioning & Bucketing — How to optimize big data queries
 6️⃣ Data Skew Handling — Join strategies & salting techniques
 7️⃣ CDC (Change Data Capture) — Incremental data loading patterns
 8️⃣ Orchestration vs Scheduling — Airflow / ADF / Prefect differences
 9️⃣ Idempotent Pipelines — Making reruns safe
 🔟 Data Quality Checks — Nulls, duplicates, constraints, drift
 1️⃣1️⃣ Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD Types) — Real warehouse scenarios
 1️⃣2️⃣ Lakehouse Architecture — Modern hybrid analytics design
If you’re preparing for Data Engineer interviews in 2026 (Accenture, TCS, Cognizant, Infosys, UST, Coforge):
 Join 2000+ learners who landed offers at TCS, Deloitte, Infosys, and more —
 not by luck, but by mastering real data engineering scenarios.
 👉 Data Engineer Interview Mega Pack 👉 https://lnkd.in/gBfGiUpf
 👉 600+ Real Data Engineer Interview Q&A 👉 https://lnkd.in/gZA3D3-D
 👉 Top 100 Real Data Engineer Questions (1–4 Years Experience) 👉 https://lnkd.in/g_2VtMR4
💡 Interview Tip:
 When answering — always explain with a real pipeline example (source → transform → load → monitor). Interviewers love practical thinking more than textbook definitions.

ai_analysis.summary: This is a promotional 2026 Data Engineer interview checklist that names 12 core concepts and briefly identifies the purpose or comparison associated with each one. It does not provide detailed definitions, technical comparisons, implementation guidance, or worked pipeline examples. The post recommends explaining interview answers with a real pipeline structured as source, transform, load, and monitor.
subtopics: Transform before load versus transform after load
Data warehouse and data lake use cases, cost, and schema strategy

interview_questions.question: In the ETL versus ELT comparison, when does transformation occur in each approach?
interview_questions.answer:
ETL performs transformation before the data is loaded.
ELT performs transformation after the data is loaded.

interview_questions.question: Which two pipeline execution styles are contrasted, and what tradeoff does the post highlight?
interview_questions.answer:
The post contrasts batch pipelines with streaming pipelines.
The highlighted tradeoff is latency versus throughput.

interview_questions.question: Which dimensional modeling approaches are contrasted, and which concerns are associated with the comparison?
interview_questions.answer:
The post contrasts star schema with snowflake schema.
It frames the comparison in terms of query performance versus normalization.

interview_questions.question: Which technique is associated with incremental data loading, and what pipeline property is associated with safe reruns?
interview_questions.answer:
Change Data Capture is associated with incremental data loading patterns.
Pipeline idempotency is associated with making reruns safe.

interview_questions.question: Which data quality checks does the checklist identify?
interview_questions.answer: The listed checks cover nulls, duplicates, constraints, and drift.

interview_questions.question: How does the checklist frame the comparison between a data warehouse and a data lake?
interview_questions.answer:
The post identifies use cases as one dimension of the comparison.
It also identifies cost and schema strategy.
The post does not provide further details about the architectural differences.
